notes: odio is also the noun 'hatred'.

sentences.translation: I used to hate this city.

gloss: front (frente a = facing, in front of)
notes: frente a = facing, opposite. al frente = at the front, in charge. la frente = forehead.

sentences.translation: I live across from the hospital.
She was in front of the door.

sentences.text: El jefe está al frente del equipo.
sentences.translation: The boss is at the head of the team.
Do you already know the baby's sex?

sentences.text: No quiero hablar de sexo con mi madre.
sentences.translation: I don't want to talk about sex with my mother.
There are people of both sexes.

notes: Means fun or amusing. 'Funny' in the sense of strange is raro.

sentences.translation: The party was a lot of fun.

notes: Also a music band: mi grupo favorito.

sentences.translation: We work in groups of four.

sentences.text: Mi grupo favorito toca esta noche.
sentences.translation: My favorite band is playing tonight.

notes: No es asunto tuyo = It's none of your business.

sentences.text: No te metas en mis asuntos.
Tengo tres mensajes de mi madre.
sentences.translation: I have three messages from my mother.

notes: encima de = on, on top of. por encima de = above. Also 'on top of that, besides'.

sentences.text: Las llaves están encima de la mesa.
sentences.translation: The keys are on the table.
It's late, and on top of that it's raining.

notes: prestar atención = to pay attention.

gloss: to be quiet; to keep quiet
notes: Usually reflexive: callarse. ¡Cállate! = Shut up! (rude between strangers).
hacer daño = to hurt. hacerse daño = to hurt yourself.

sentences.translation: I don't want to hurt you.
The fire caused a lot of damage.

notes: ¿Qué sucede? = What's going on? Same meaning as pasar and ocurrir.
cambiar de = to change (one thing for another): cambiar de trabajo.
al día siguiente = the next day.
After a negative: no A sino B = not A but B. Different from pero.

sentences.translation: I don't want money, I want help.

sentences.text: No fue él, sino su hermano.
sentences.translation: It wasn't him, it was his brother.

notes: médica = female doctor. As an adjective: medical (atención médica).

sentences.translation: You have to go to the doctor.

sentences.text: No hables con la boca llena.
sentences.translation: Don't talk with your mouth full.

notes: cometer un error = to make a mistake.

sentences.text: Creo que hay un error en la cuenta.
sentences.translation: I think there's a mistake in the bill.

notes: Stronger than nunca. nunca jamás = never ever.

sentences.text: Es lo mejor que he visto jamás.
sentences.translation: It's the best thing I've ever seen.

notes: False friend: largo means long, not large (grande).
¡Qué pena! = What a shame! vale la pena = it's worth it. In Latin America pena also means embarrassment.

sentences.translation: It makes me sad to see you like this.

notes: en voz alta = out loud. en voz baja = quietly.

sentences.translation: What plans do you have for the future?
I have no secrets from you.

notes: ir al baño = to go to the bathroom. darse un baño = to take a bath.

sentences.translation: I need to go to the bathroom.
The restrooms are at the back.

notes: No plural after a number: dos mil = two thousand. miles = thousands.

sentences.text: Te lo he dicho mil veces.
sentences.translation: I've told you a thousand times.

notes: novia = girlfriend or bride. los novios = the couple; the bride and groom.

sentences.text: La novia lleva un vestido blanco.
sentences.translation: The bride is wearing a white dress.

notes: Goes before the noun: mi propia casa = my own house.

sentences.text: Lo vi con mis propios ojos.
sentences.translation: I saw it with my own eyes.

notes: tener sueño = to be sleepy.

sentences.translation: Last night I had a strange dream.

sentences.text: Es el trabajo de mis sueños.

notes: a la fuerza = by force. no tener fuerzas = to have no strength left.

sentences.translation: They took him out by force.

notes: Agrees in gender: ambos chicos, ambas chicas.
dolor de cabeza = headache.

sentences.translation: He's in a lot of pain.

notes: Works like gustar: me encanta = I love it. me encantaría = I'd love to.

sentences.translation: I'd love to go with you.

notes: ¿Qué edad tienes? = How old are you?

sentences.translation: At your age, I was working.

notes: a pie = on foot. de pie = standing.
ganar dinero = to earn money.

sentences.translation: She earns a lot of money.

notes: tomar el aire = to get some fresh air.

sentences.text: El aire está muy limpio aquí.
sentences.translation: The air is very clean here.

gloss: to be sorry about; to regret
notes: Lo lamento = I'm sorry (a little more formal than lo siento).

sentences.text: Hubo dos asesinatos en esta calle.
sentences.translation: There were two murders on this street.

notes: Asks about direction: ¿Adónde vas? = Where are you going? Also written a dónde.

sentences.translation: Where are you going so early?
I don't know where to go.

notes: ¡Disculpe! = Excuse me! (formal). disculpa is also the noun 'apology'. disculparse = to apologize.

sentences.translation: You have to apologize to her.
I have a lot of appointments today.

sentences.text: Nuestra primera cita fue en un café.
sentences.translation: Our first date was at a café.

notes: Masculine despite the -a: el sistema.

sentences.text: Hay un problema con el sistema.
sentences.translation: There's a problem with the system.

notes: Mucho gusto = Nice to meet you. con gusto = gladly.
Before a noun it often means 'unfortunate': ¡pobre chico!
de negocios = on business.

sentences.text: Mi padre está de viaje de negocios.
sentences.translation: My father is on a business trip.
What do you have in mind?
She has a very open mind.

notes: Agrees with the thing owned: el libro es tuyo, la casa es tuya.
el campo = the countryside (as opposed to the city).

sentences.text: Detrás de la casa hay campos.
sentences.translation: There are fields behind the house.

sentences.text: Los niños juegan en el campo de fútbol.
sentences.translation: The kids are playing on the soccer field.

notes: More formal than después de / detrás de. día tras día = day after day.

sentences.text: Día tras día, espera su carta.
sentences.translation: Day after day, she waits for his letter.

sentences.text: La puerta se cerró tras él.

notes: Used in Spain. Latin America uses ustedes for every plural 'you'.

sentences.translation: Are you guys going to the party?

notes: For things and plans. A person works = trabajar.
Feminine despite the -o: la foto (short for la fotografía). sacar una foto = to take a photo.

sentences.translation: Can you take a photo of us?

sentences.text: Tengo muchas fotos de mi hija.
sentences.translation: I have lots of photos of my daughter.

notes: abogada = female lawyer.

sentences.translation: I want to talk to my lawyer.

notes: alrededor de = around (a place), or about (a number).

sentences.text: Hay árboles alrededor de la casa.
sentences.translation: There are trees around the house.

notes: la próxima vez = next time. la próxima semana = next week.

sentences.text: El próximo tren sale a las seis.
sentences.translation: The next train leaves at six.

sentences.text: La película termina a las once.

notes: No preposition: pagar la cena = to pay for dinner. pago is also the noun 'payment'.
Also a noun: el personal = the staff.
se me ocurre = it occurs to me, I've got an idea.
la mitad de = half (of). a mitad de = halfway through.

sentences.text: La mitad de la gente se fue.

notes: Usually singular: el pelo = (all of) your hair.

sentences.text: Hay pelos de perro en la cama.
sentences.translation: There's dog hair on the bed.

notes: Also an adjective: official.

sentences.text: Mi abuelo era oficial del ejército.
sentences.translation: My grandfather was an army officer.

notes: Both a business and being with someone.
un montón (de) = a lot (of), informal.

sentences.translation: I have a ton of work.

sentences.text: Hay montones de ropa en la cama.
sentences.translation: There are piles of clothes on the bed.

notes: The evening meal, usually late in Spain.

sentences.text: La cena es a las nueve.

notes: Only in a través de = through, across; by means of.

sentences.text: Lo vi a través de la ventana.
sentences.translation: I saw it through the window.

sentences.text: Hablamos a través de la puerta.
Lo supe a través de un amigo.
sentences.translation: I found out through a friend.

sentences.text: Hay muchos accidentes en esta carretera.
sentences.translation: There are a lot of accidents on this road.

notes: In a shop, la caja = the checkout, the till.

sentences.text: Pon los libros en esas cajas.
sentences.translation: Put the books in those boxes.

sentences.text: Pague en la caja, por favor.

notes: ¡Tranquilo! = Relax! / Don't worry!

sentences.translation: Relax, everything's going to be fine!

notes: Common in Spain; Latin America also says lindo.

sentences.translation: You have a very nice house.

notes: ¡Hasta la vista! = See you! a primera vista = at first sight.

sentences.text: Una habitación con vistas al mar.
sentences.translation: A room with a sea view.

notes: Rude when said to a person.

sentences.translation: I only wrote you a few lines.

notes: Damas y caballeros = Ladies and gentlemen.

sentences.text: El caballero salvó a la princesa.
La tienda cierra a las ocho.
Hay muchas tiendas en esta calle.
sentences.translation: There are lots of shops on this street.

notes: ir de compras = to go shopping.

sentences.translation: Where did you buy that dress?

sentences.text: Le compré flores a mi madre.

notes: el centro = the town center, downtown.

sentences.translation: We're going into town this afternoon.

sentences.text: Está en el centro de la foto.
sentences.translation: He's in the middle of the photo.

notes: a salvo = safe. Also a form of salvar: yo salvo = I save.

sentences.text: Abrimos todos los días, salvo los lunes.
sentences.translation: We're open every day except Mondays.

notes: hace sol = it's sunny.

sentences.text: El sol sale a las siete.

notes: Milder than estúpido. No seas tonto = Don't be silly.

sentences.translation: Do you take me for a fool?

notes: Feminine, but el hambre (stressed a-). tener hambre = to be hungry.

sentences.text: La cena está en la mesa.
Una mesa para dos, por favor.
Las respuestas están al final del libro.
sentences.translation: The answers are at the end of the book.

notes: jugar a las cartas = to play cards. la carta = the menu in a restaurant.

sentences.translation: Could you bring us the menu, please?
You're asking me for impossible things.
It's impossible to talk to him.
I just want a normal life.

notes: Irregular: traigo, traje (preterite). traje is also the noun 'suit'.

sentences.translation: We're going in the right direction.
You gave me two different addresses.
It's a pleasure to meet you.
Are you traveling for business or pleasure?

notes: en barco = by boat.

sentences.text: Todo está blanco por la nieve.
